es: Reconocer repetición, contraste, pregunta retórica y lenguaje emotivo en anuncios y eslóganes, y explicar el efecto de cada técnica sobre el público.

vocabulary.es: emotivo, que apela a los sentimientos

teaching.en: The slogan 'Clean rivers, clean streets, clean lives' relies on repetition: the same word returns three times, which makes the message memorable.
teaching.es: El eslogan «Ríos limpios, calles limpias, vidas limpias» se apoya en la repetición: la misma palabra vuelve tres veces, lo que hace el mensaje fácil de recordar.
teaching.explanationEs: Repetición: la misma palabra o estructura reaparece para que el eslogan se grabe.
segments: The slogan 'Clean rivers, clean streets, clean lives' relies on repetition:
the same word returns three times, which makes the message memorable.
teaching.audioText: The slogan 'Clean rivers, clean streets, clean lives' relies on repetition: the same word returns three times, which makes the message memorable.

teaching.en: An advert built on contrast sets two opposite ideas side by side, such as the slow old bus and the fast new one, to make the choice obvious.
teaching.es: Un anuncio construido sobre el contraste coloca dos ideas opuestas lado a lado, como el autobús viejo y lento y el nuevo y rápido, para que la elección resulte obvia.
teaching.explanationEs: Contraste: dos ideas opuestas en la misma frase o imagen destacan la opción que interesa.
segments: An advert built on contrast sets two opposite ideas side by side, such as
the slow old bus and the fast new one, to make the choice obvious.
teaching.audioText: An advert built on contrast sets two opposite ideas side by side, such as the slow old bus and the fast new one, to make the choice obvious.

teaching.en: A rhetorical question does not expect an answer, because the audience is meant to reach the obvious conclusion without being told.
teaching.es: Una pregunta retórica no espera respuesta, porque se pretende que el público llegue solo a la conclusión obvia sin que se la digan.
teaching.explanationEs: Pregunta retórica: se formula para pensar, no para recibir una respuesta.
segments: A rhetorical question does not expect an answer, because the audience
is meant to reach the obvious conclusion without being told.
teaching.audioText: A rhetorical question does not expect an answer, because the audience is meant to reach the obvious conclusion without being told.

teaching.en: Emotive language, such as shameful or heartbreaking, is another technique that persuades readers by appealing to feelings rather than facts.
teaching.es: El lenguaje emotivo, como «vergonzoso» o «desgarrador», es otra técnica que persuade a los lectores apelando a los sentimientos más que a los hechos.
teaching.explanationEs: Emotive = que apela a la emoción; suele sustituir datos por sentimientos.
segments: Emotive language, such as shameful or heartbreaking, is another technique
that persuades readers by appealing to feelings rather than facts.
teaching.audioText: Emotive language, such as shameful or heartbreaking, is another technique that persuades readers by appealing to feelings rather than facts.

teaching.en: Each technique has a different effect on the reader, so a good analysis names the technique first and then explains what it makes the audience feel.
teaching.es: Cada técnica tiene un efecto distinto en el lector, así que un buen análisis nombra primero la técnica y luego explica qué hace sentir al público.
teaching.explanationEs: Al analizar: primero la técnica y después su efecto sobre el público.
segments: Each technique has a different effect on the reader, so a good analysis
names the technique first and then explains what it makes the audience feel.
teaching.audioText: Each technique has a different effect on the reader, so a good analysis names the technique first and then explains what it makes the audience feel.

teaching.en: Repetition helps to put emphasis on the central idea, which is why advertisers try to persuade us with short, memorable phrases.
teaching.es: La repetición ayuda a poner énfasis en la idea central, y por eso los publicistas intentan persuadirnos con frases breves y fáciles de recordar.
teaching.explanationEs: Put emphasis on + nombre: destacar una idea; emphasis es incontable.
segments: Repetition helps to put emphasis on the central idea, which is
why advertisers try to persuade us with short, memorable phrases.
teaching.audioText: Repetition helps to put emphasis on the central idea, which is why advertisers try to persuade us with short, memorable phrases.

prompt.es: Identifica la técnica principal del eslogan de la escuela de idiomas.

choices.text: It repeats the same word at the end of each short sentence.
It sets two opposite ideas side by side to show a choice.
It asks the reader a question that has an obvious answer.

feedback.es: More cierra cada frase corta: es repetición, no contraste ni pregunta retórica.

hint.es: Fíjate en la palabra que vuelve a aparecer en cada frase.

origin.text: A language school has put this slogan on every poster in the underground: Read more. Learn more. Be more.

prompt.es: Completa: «El anuncio usa el contraste para mostrar la diferencia.»

feedback.es: El contraste enfrenta dos ideas opuestas (lento y ruidoso frente a rápido y silencioso); en inglés se llama contrast.

hint.es: Se parece mucho a la palabra española.

origin.text: The advert compares the old bus with the new one: the first is slow and noisy, the second is fast and silent. It uses ___ to show the difference.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El eslogan usa la repetición para hacerlo memorable.»

answer.text: The slogan uses repetition to make it memorable

feedback.es: Se nombra la técnica y el efecto va al final con to + verbo.

hint.es: Primero la técnica; al final, to + efecto.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada eslogan con su técnica.

pairs: Clean town, clean park, clean home.
Old cars are noisy. New cars are silent.
Who needs more noise in the city?

feedback.es: Una palabra repetida, dos ideas opuestas, una pregunta sin respuesta y adjetivos cargados de emoción son las cuatro señales.

pairs: Clean town, clean park, clean home.
Old cars are noisy. New cars are silent.
Who needs more noise in the city?

prompt.es: Elige el efecto de la pregunta retórica del anuncio.

choices.text: It asks the reader to send an answer to the council.
It makes the reader feel that the answer is obvious.
It invites the reader to compare two different proposals.

feedback.es: La pregunta no espera respuesta: hace pensar al lector que la conclusión es obvia, y ese es su efecto.

origin.text: Why should we keep losing our green spaces to car parks, when every child needs somewhere safe to play?

prompt.es: Explica en una frase el efecto de la repetición del eslogan.

answer.text: The repetition of fresh makes the slogan easy to remember.
accepted: The repetition of fresh makes the slogan easy to remember.
The repetition of the word fresh makes the slogan memorable.
Repeating the word fresh makes the message easy to remember.
The repetition of fresh puts emphasis on the idea and makes it memorable.

feedback.es: El efecto de repetir una palabra es que el eslogan resulte fácil de recordar y refuerce la idea.

origin.text: Fresh food, fresh ideas, fresh start.

prompt.es: Escucha el pódcast y elige la técnica del cartel principal.

choices.text: A contrast between cheap trains and expensive cars.
Repetition of one word across several short phrases.
A rhetorical question that invites obvious agreement.

feedback.es: El cartel principal pregunta quién disfruta del tráfico: una pregunta retórica. La repetición de free pertenece a los carteles pequeños.

origin.audio: In this week's media podcast, a teacher examines a campaign that urges commuters to leave their cars at home. The main poster asks, Who enjoys sitting in traffic? Nobody answers, of course, because the audience already agrees. Smaller posters repeat the word free three times: free seats, free air, free time. The teacher admits that the campaign is memorable, yet she notes that it never mentions the cost of a train ticket.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué da a entender la profesora al final.

choices.text: That the campaign is memorable but leaves out a key fact.
That the campaign works because it says nothing about costs.
That cheaper tickets would make the campaign stronger.

feedback.es: Con yet señala un reparo: la campaña se recuerda, pero omite el precio del pasaje; no dice que funcione gracias a ello ni que los pasajes deban bajar.

origin.audio: In this week's media podcast, a teacher examines a campaign that urges commuters to leave their cars at home. The main poster asks, Who enjoys sitting in traffic? Nobody answers, of course, because the audience already agrees. Smaller posters repeat the word free three times: free seats, free air, free time. The teacher admits that the campaign is memorable, yet she notes that it never mentions the cost of a train ticket.

prompt.es: Completa: «Su lenguaje es muy emotivo porque busca conmover, no dar datos.»

feedback.es: Emotive describe el lenguaje que apela a los sentimientos en lugar de a los hechos.

origin.text: The poster uses words such as shameful and heartbreaking. Its language is highly ___ because it aims to move the reader's feelings rather than to provide facts.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Los publicistas ponen énfasis en los sentimientos más que en los hechos.»

answer.text: Advertisers put emphasis on feelings rather than facts

feedback.es: Put emphasis on + nombre: así se nombra lo que un anuncio destaca; rather than contrapone los hechos.

prompt.es: Elige la técnica del eslogan de tres frases cortas.

choices.text: Contrast between happy children and empty parks.
Repetition of the same word to open each phrase.
A rhetorical question aimed at the parents reading it.

feedback.es: Every abre cada frase corta: es repetición. La pregunta final es otra técnica distinta del eslogan de tres frases.

origin.text: Every child. Every park. Every day. This is the slogan of a playground campaign, which also asks parents: Would you want your child to grow up without a place to play?

prompt.es: Elige con qué propósito incluye el anuncio la pregunta sobre las dos horas.

choices.text: To ask readers how long their journey really takes.
To prove that the bus is faster than driving.
To make readers feel that driving wastes their time.

feedback.es: La pregunta no busca una cifra: quiere que el lector sienta que conducir es una pérdida de tiempo, y por eso es retórica.

origin.text: Switch to the bus, and you will have your mornings back. Why should anyone spend two hours a day in a queue of cars? The city has given you the choice; now make it.

prompt.es: Completa: «El autor quiere persuadir al lector de que use el autobús cada día.»

feedback.es: Persuade someone to + verbo: persuadir a alguien de que haga algo.

origin.text: The writer wants to ___ the reader to take the bus every day, so the advert uses feelings as well as facts.
